title: IRIS: A 8.55 mJ/frame Spatial Computing SoC for Real-time Interactable-Rendering and Surface-aware-Modeling with 3D Gaussian Splatting
problem: Real-time spatial computing with 3D Gaussian Splatting requires specialized hardware for low-latency, energy-efficient rendering and surface modeling.
motivation: XR/spatial computing demands real-time rendering at 8-12 fps while maintaining low power envelope for mobile devices, driving need for specialized SoCs.
method: IRIS is a domain-specific SoC optimized for 3D Gaussian Splatting with dedicated pipelines for Gaussian rasterization, differentiable rendering, and surface reconstruction, achieving energy efficiency through algorithmic optimization.
key_novelty: First SoC co-designed specifically for 3D Gaussian Splatting with optimized rendering and surface-modeling pipelines.
contributions: Specialized SoC architecture for Gaussian Splatting rendering
Real-time interactable rendering with surface awareness
